name: Alabama
description: Alabama requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles. The state has a lemon law that covers new vehicles purchased or leased in Alabama, and does not require emissions testing statewide.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
lemonLawSummary: Alabama gives a new-car buyer a lemon-law rights period of one year or 12,000 miles, whichever comes first, under Ala. Code §§ 8-20A-1(8) and 8-20A-2. The repair presumption is measured over 24 months or 24,000 miles, and at least one repair attempt has to fall inside that first year or 12,000 miles. The law treats the car as having had a reasonable number of attempts after three repairs of the same problem plus a final try by the manufacturer, or after 30 calendar days out of service, counting that final try. Before a lawsuit, send the manufacturer certified mail; once the presumption is already in place, the manufacturer gets seven calendar days to name a shop and 14 calendar days after you drop the car off to fix it.
registrationNotes: A designated agent and a licensing official may each add a $1.50 commission. Some counties add a local fee. Ala. Code § 40-12-242 sets the automobile fee.

name: Alaska
description: Alaska has some of the most unique vehicle ownership requirements in the nation. While liability insurance is mandatory, the state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections for most vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Under AS 45.45.320, Alaska measures the presumption during the express warranty or the year after delivery to the original owner, whichever ends first, and the statute sets no mileage cap. Three repairs of the same problem, if it is still there, or 30 business days in the shop, is enough attempts. Days when the shop cannot work for reasons outside its control do not count. To demand a refund or replacement, mail written notice before 60 days have passed after the warranty or that one-year period ends; the manufacturer then has 30 days to try one last repair.
registrationNotes: Registration is biennial. There is no state sales tax. Some municipalities charge a local tax on a vehicle purchase.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Arizona
description: Arizona vehicle owners benefit from relatively low insurance minimums but must comply with emissions testing in the Phoenix and Tucson metro areas. The state offers incentives for electric and alternative fuel vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Arizona measures lemon-law repairs under Ariz. Rev. Stat. §§ 44-1262 and 44-1264 during the shorter of the express warranty or two years and 24,000 miles after the car was delivered. The presumption is four repairs of the same defect that still exists, or 30 calendar days the car spends out of service. Before that presumption can be used, the manufacturer has to have received direct written notice of the defect. It also has to have had a chance to repair the car.
emissionsDetails: The Phoenix area tests every two years. The Tucson area tests annually. The OBD test fee is $16.15 in both areas. The older tailpipe test is $15.20 in Phoenix and $12.25 in Tucson. The Arizona Department of Environmental Quality publishes these fees. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
registrationFeeRange: $8 base fee plus vehicle license tax
registrationNotes: The vehicle license tax starts at 60 percent of the manufacturer base retail price. The value then drops 16.25 percent each year. The minimum tax is $10.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Arkansas
description: Arkansas requires liability insurance and has a lemon law protecting new vehicle buyers. The state does not mandate emissions testing or a periodic safety inspection.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Arkansas runs its quality period to 24 months or 24,000 miles, whichever is later, in Ark. Code §§ 4-90-403(12), 4-90-406, and 4-90-410. After three tries at the same problem that substantially impairs the car, or one try at a problem likely to cause death or serious injury, send certified or registered mail so the manufacturer can make a final repair. A presumption also arises if that path was followed and the problem remains, if the car spent 30 calendar days in the shop, or if there were five or more attempts on separate occasions at problems that together substantially impair use and value. The manufacturer has ten days after the letter to offer a shop and ten days after you deliver the car to fix it; if it misses those deadlines, the final-attempt requirement drops and the presumption can no longer be rebutted.
registrationFeeRange: $17 up to 3,000 lb, $25 from 3,001 to 4,500 lb, or $30 above 4,500 lb
registrationNotes: That plate amount is the validation decal. A tag transfer is $1. An annual personal property assessment applies.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: California
description: California has the most comprehensive vehicle regulations in the country, including strict emissions standards, generous EV incentives, and strong consumer protection laws including a robust lemon law.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $15,000 bodily injury per person / $30,000 bodily injury per accident / $5,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: California's Tanner presumption is Cal. Civ. Code § 1793.22. It applies during the first 18 months after delivery or the first 18,000 miles, whichever comes first. Within that time, two repairs of a defect likely to cause death or serious bodily injury, four repairs of the same defect, or more than 30 calendar days in the shop is a reasonable number of attempts. Direct notice to the manufacturer is required for the two-repair and four-repair counts only when the warranty or owner's manual clearly told the buyer to send it.
emissionsDetails: California requires biennial smog checks for vehicles older than eight model years in most areas. The state sets its own emissions standards through CARB, which are stricter than federal standards. Testing typically costs $30-$70. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
evIncentiveDetails: California's statewide CVRP rebate closed November 8, 2023. Income-qualified residents who scrap an older vehicle can apply for Clean Cars 4 All (cleancars4all.arb.ca.gov) before buying, and many California utilities offer EV charger rebates and EV rates.
registrationNotes: The registration fee includes a $3 alternative fuel and technology fee. That title amount is the transfer fee. A title-only application is $28. Replacement plates are $28. A separate CHP fee is $34. The vehicle license fee is 0.65 percent of value.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A model year 2020 or later zero-emission vehicle pays a $121 road improvement fee at renewal. That fee is not charged on the first registration of a new zero-emission vehicle bought from a licensed dealer.

name: Colorado
description: Colorado combines mandatory liability insurance with emissions testing in the Denver metro area. The state is a leader in EV incentives, offering substantial tax credits for electric vehicle purchases.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: For vehicles sold or leased on or after August 7, 2024, Colo. Rev. Stat. § 42-10-103, as amended by SB 24-192, uses the first two years or 24,000 miles. Three repairs of the same problem, two repairs of a safety-based problem, or 24 business days out of service is the presumption, and the problem has to still be there. The manufacturer needs prior written notice by certified mail and then has ten business days after receiving it to try a cure. That cure counts as one repair.
emissionsDetails: Gasoline vehicles in all or parts of Adams, Arapahoe, Boulder, Broomfield, Denver, Douglas, Jefferson, Larimer, and Weld counties are tested every two years. The newest vehicles are exempt for seven model years. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
evIncentiveDetails: Colorado offers a state EV tax credit of $750 in 2026 for new EVs with an MSRP up to $80,000, plus an additional $2,500 for EVs with an MSRP under $35,000 (Colorado Energy Office). Dealers can apply the credit at purchase. Leases must be at least two years.
registrationFeeRange: Based on weight and specific ownership tax
registrationNotes: Specific ownership tax declines as the vehicle ages. Registration is annual.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: The Colorado DMV lists a plug-in electric vehicle fee of $63.05. It also lists a road-usage charge of $26 for a battery-electric vehicle from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.

name: Connecticut
description: Connecticut requires emissions testing for most vehicles and has strong consumer protection laws. The state mandates relatively high insurance minimums compared to the national average.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Connecticut's lemon law is Conn. Gen. Stat. § 42-179. The ordinary presumption runs during the first two years or 24,000 miles: four repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service, if the problem continues. A defect likely to cause death or serious injury uses a shorter window, the express warranty or one year after delivery, and it takes two repairs. You do not have to notify the manufacturer unless the warranty or the owner's manual clearly says written notice is required.
emissionsDetails: Connecticut tests registered vehicles every two years. The emissions test fee is $20. Vehicles younger than four model years are exempt. Model year 2001 and older vehicles are exempt. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
evIncentiveDetails: Connecticut's CHEAPR program offers $1,500 for new battery EVs (from October 15, 2026) and $500 for plug-in hybrids at participating dealers. Income-qualified Rebate+ buyers can receive up to $4,500 on a new battery EV.
registrationNotes: The same passenger row lists a $10 administrative fee and a $15 Clean Air Act fee. The Passport to the Parks fee on that row is $24. A vehicle four years old or newer pays a $40 emissions exemption fee. A vehicle with a certificate of origin pays a $15 greenhouse gas fee.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Delaware
description: Delaware requires liability insurance and biennial vehicle inspections. The state has no sales tax on vehicle purchases, which can represent significant savings for car buyers.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Del. Code tit. 6, § 5004 covers a new car for the warranty term or the first year after delivery, whichever ends first. Mileage does not cut that period short. The presumption is in place when substantially the same problem has been repaired four times and is still there, or when the car has been out of service for more than 30 calendar days. Use it against the manufacturer only after the manufacturer got a direct written notice and a chance to fix the car.
emissionsDetails: The emissions test covers New Castle, Kent, and Sussex counties. Vehicles in the first seven model years are excluded. Model year 1996 and newer gasoline vehicles use an OBD-II test. The inspection is free for Delaware residents. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: Delaware inspects vehicles every two years before renewal. Vehicles in the first seven model years are excluded. The DMV conducts the inspection. Required inspections are free for Delaware residents.
registrationNotes: The document fee is 5.25 percent of the purchase price or NADA value. A duplicate plate with a sticker is $10. A plug-in hybrid under 6,000 pounds pays an additional $85 a year. A non-plug-in hybrid under 6,000 pounds pays an additional $60 a year.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric or fuel-cell vehicle under 6,000 pounds pays an additional $110 a year.

name: Florida
description: Florida is a no-fault insurance state, meaning your own insurance covers your injuries regardless of who caused the accident. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $10,000 personal injury protection (PIP) / $10,000 property damage liability. Bodily injury liability is only required if the driver has had license or registration suspended.
lemonLawSummary: Fla. Stat. §§ 681.102(9) and 681.104 give a rights period of 24 months after delivery, and the statute does not use a mileage cap. The presumption is three repairs of the same problem plus a final attempt by the manufacturer, if that attempt is undertaken, or 30 cumulative days out of service, 60 for a recreational vehicle. When the car has been out of service for 15 days, send written notice by registered or express mail so the manufacturer can inspect or repair. After three attempts on the same problem, a separate written notice gives the manufacturer one last repair.
registrationNotes: The initial registration fee is $225. Florida calls that charge the new wheels on the road fee. An original used electronic title is $85.25. A lien fee of $2 may be added.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Georgia
description: Georgia requires liability insurance and emissions testing in the metro Atlanta area. The state replaced its traditional sales tax on vehicles with a one-time title ad valorem tax (TAVT).
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Georgia's lemon law, O.C.G.A. §§ 10-1-782 and 10-1-784, ends the rights period at two years or 24,000 miles, whichever comes first. One unsuccessful repair of a serious safety defect, three unsuccessful repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service counts as a reasonable number of attempts. After that, notify the manufacturer. It then has 28 days from receiving the notice to try one last repair.
emissionsDetails: Gasoline vehicles in Cherokee, Clayton, Cobb, Coweta, DeKalb, Douglas, Fayette, Forsyth, Fulton, Gwinnett, Henry, Paulding, and Rockdale counties are covered. Covered light-duty vehicles are the newest 24 model years. A new vehicle is exempt until the inspection term three years after the model year. The station fee is at least $10 and no more than $25. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
registrationNotes: The title ad valorem tax is 7 percent of fair market value on a standard purchase. A new resident pays 3 percent. A replacement plate or decal is $8.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Hawaii
description: Hawaii requires all registered vehicles to pass a periodic safety inspection. The state has mandatory no-fault insurance and offers growing incentives for electric vehicles as part of its clean energy goals.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $20,000 bodily injury per person / $40,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / $10,000 PIP
lemonLawSummary: Hawaii's lemon law, Haw. Rev. Stat. §§ 481I-2 and 481I-3, sets the rights period as the express warranty, two years, or 24,000 miles, whichever comes first. Three exams or repairs of the same problem, one exam or repair of a problem likely to cause death or serious injury, or 30 business days out of service, is the presumption. The manufacturer has to have received a written report and a reasonable chance to repair. A dealer also notifies the manufacturer after a second report or after the car has been out more than 20 business days.
emissionsDetails: Hawaii's periodic inspection is a safety check under HRS § 286-26. It is not an emissions test. The inspection looks at the exhaust system because a noncompliant muffler fails the safety check.
safetyInspectionDetails: Hawaii requires a periodic safety inspection under HRS § 286-26. Most passenger vehicles are inspected every 12 months. A new vehicle does not need that annual inspection until two years after its first inspection. Since July 1, 2025, the fee is $25.75 for automobiles and trucks.
registrationFeeRange: $46 a year plus county weight tax
registrationNotes: Honolulu charges $10 to transfer a title within 30 days. Hawaii County charges $5. Alternative-fuel vehicles pay an extra $50. An electric vehicle is excluded from that alternative-fuel surcharge. HRS § 249-31 sets the state registration fee.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Idaho
description: Idaho has relatively low insurance requirements and does not mandate emissions testing or safety inspections for most personal vehicles. The state has a straightforward registration process.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Idaho Code § 48-903 looks at the express warranty, two years, or 24,000 miles, whichever date comes first. If the problem was first reported during the warranty, repair attempts within three years of delivery can still support a refund or replacement. Four repairs of the same problem, 30 business days out of service, or one repair of a complete brake or steering failure likely to cause death or serious injury, is the presumption, and the manufacturer still gets one chance to repair that brake or steering failure. The four-repair and 30-day paths apply against the manufacturer only after written notice and a chance to cure.
registrationFeeRange: $69 at 1 or 2 years, $57 at 3 to 6 years, or $45 at 7 or more years
registrationNotes: The title amount is the state base. Counties add an administrative fee. A plug-in hybrid pays an additional $75 a year.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle pays an additional $140 a year under Idaho Code § 49-457.

name: Illinois
description: Illinois requires liability insurance and emissions testing in the Chicago metro area and Metro East St. Louis. The state has a strong lemon law and offers incentives for electric vehicle purchases.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Illinois sets its own lemon-law period in 815 ILCS 380/2 and 380/3: one year or 12,000 miles after delivery, whichever comes first. Four repairs of the same problem that still exists, or 30 business days out of service, is the presumption inside that period. The manufacturer must have received direct written notice from the buyer, or from someone acting for the buyer. It also needs a chance to correct the defect before the presumption applies.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is required for most gasoline vehicles registered in Cook, DuPage, and Lake counties, and in designated parts of Kane, Kendall, McHenry, Will, Madison, Monroe, and St. Clair counties, under the Vehicle Emissions Inspection Law of 2005. Most 1996 and newer gasoline passenger vehicles are tested after they are four years old, on the biennial schedule that matches the license-plate year. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
evIncentiveDetails: The Illinois EPA EV rebate cycle runs August 1 to December 31, 2026: $2,000, or $4,000 for low-income applicants. Applications must be made within 180 days of purchase.
registrationNotes: Registration is annual.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle pays an additional $100 a year. Annual renewal of that plate is listed at $251.

name: Indiana
description: Indiana requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles and has a lemon law covering new car purchases. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Indiana calls the coverage a term of protection under Ind. Code §§ 24-5-13-7, 24-5-13-8, and 24-5-13-15. It ends at the earlier of 18 months or 18,000 miles, and the buyer has to report the problem before that term runs out. Four repairs that leave the problem in place, or 30 business days out of service with the problem still there, counts as a reasonable number of attempts. If the manufacturer made the disclosure in § 24-5-13-9, the buyer notifies the manufacturer of the claim first.
registrationNotes: The annual excise tax is based on value and age. A transfer or replacement plate is $9.50. The fee chart lists a hybrid supplemental fee of $81.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: The fee chart lists an electric-vehicle supplemental fee of $242.

name: Iowa
description: Iowa requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing but does have some of the most affordable vehicle registration fees in the nation.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $20,000 bodily injury per person / $40,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Iowa's lemon law, Iowa Code §§ 322G.2 and 322G.4, uses the written warranty, two years, or 24,000 miles, whichever expires first, and it counts calendar days. The presumption is three exams or repairs of the same problem plus a final attempt if one is undertaken, one exam or repair of a problem likely to cause death or serious injury plus that final attempt, or 30 days out of service. You can send written notice after 20 cumulative days out of service, after three attempts, or after one attempt on a dangerous defect. The manufacturer then has a final chance to conform the car, including 10 cumulative out-of-service days after the 20-day notice.
registrationFeeRange: 1% of value plus 40 cents per 100 pounds
registrationNotes: The fee for a new registration is $10 plus 5 percent of the purchase price. The value portion decreases after seven model years. The annual fee is $50 once the vehicle is 12 model years or older.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A battery-electric vehicle pays $130. A plug-in hybrid under 10,000 pounds pays $65.

name: Kansas
description: Kansas requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing. A VIN inspection applies when a vehicle is titled from another state.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Kansas applies Kan. Stat. Ann. § 50-645 during the express warranty or the first year after delivery, whichever ends sooner, and the statute sets no mileage limit. Four repairs of the same problem, 30 calendar days out of service, or ten attempts on any problems that substantially impair use and value, is the presumption. Those counts matter once the manufacturer has actual notice of the trouble. Get that notice to the manufacturer while the warranty or the one-year period is still open.
emissionsDetails: The Kansas Highway Patrol says the state does not require emissions testing, and Johnson County tells vehicle owners the same thing.
safetyInspectionDetails: Kansas does not require a periodic safety inspection for ordinary passenger vehicles. A VIN inspection by the Highway Patrol, or a designee, is required before titling a vehicle that comes in on an out-of-state title. Salvage and rebuilt vehicles have a separate inspection.
registrationFeeRange: $30 at 4,500 lb or less, or $40 above that weight
registrationNotes: Personal property tax is also assessed on vehicles. Kansas statute 8-143 lists $70 for an electric hybrid and $100 for a plug-in electric hybrid.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An all-electric passenger vehicle is registered at $165 under Kansas statute 8-143.

name: Kentucky
description: Kentucky requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing but mandates personal property taxes on all vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Kentucky's window under Ky. Rev. Stat. § 367.842 is the first 12 months or 12,000 miles, whichever arrives first. The presumption looks at that same defect: four repair attempts, or 30 calendar days the car is out of service because of it. When a reasonable number of attempts still leaves the car unrepaired, the buyer puts the problem in writing to the manufacturer.
registrationNotes: County clerks list a $21 yearly renewal at the counter. A 6 percent usage tax applies to a purchase. Personal property tax is assessed each year.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A vehicle with plug-in charging pays a base ownership fee of $120 under KRS 138.475. The statute adjusts that amount.

name: Louisiana
description: Louisiana requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. Act 701 stops inspection-sticker citations for personal vehicles from June 30, 2026 through January 1, 2027, when that sticker requirement ends outside federal inspection-and-maintenance parishes.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $15,000 bodily injury per person / $30,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: La. Rev. Stat. § 51:1943 gives the manufacturer the warranty period or one year after delivery, and the presumption uses the date that arrives first. The section does not cut the period off by mileage. Four repairs of the same problem, or 45 calendar days out of service, is the presumption, and § 51:1944 uses those same numbers for the refund or replacement. If the manufacturer misses the response or repair time in § 51:1943(A), it loses the right to a final attempt.
safetyInspectionDetails: Act 701 prohibits inspection-sticker citations for personal non-commercial vehicles from June 30, 2026 through January 1, 2027. The sticker requirement for those vehicles ends January 1, 2027, except in parishes that stay in a federal inspection-and-maintenance program until EPA approves a change. Commercial vehicles, school buses, and certain farm vehicles still have inspection rules.
registrationNotes: Automobile plates are sold for two years at one-tenth of 1 percent of value per year, with a minimum value of $10,000. The top row of the published table is for a value of $40,500 to $41,499. A handling fee of $8 applies. A local fee may apply and will not exceed $6.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Maine
description: Maine requires liability insurance and annual vehicle inspections. The state has a strong lemon law and participates in the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, promoting cleaner transportation.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Maine's repair duty in Me. Rev. Stat. tit. 10, § 1163 runs during the express warranties, three years, or 18,000 miles, whichever comes first. Three repairs of the same problem, one repair of a serious brake or steering failure, or 15 business days out of service, is the presumption. Write the manufacturer that you want a refund or a replacement. It then has a final repair chance during the seven business days after it receives the letter, and that letter can go out after a single brake or steering failure.
emissionsDetails: Maine follows California's CARB emissions standards and requires OBD-II emissions testing in Cumberland County for vehicles older than the current plus one model year. Testing is annual. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: Maine requires an annual inspection. The station may not charge more than $12.50 for a standard inspection. A Cumberland County enhanced inspection may not exceed $15.50 for a pre-1996 vehicle or $18.50 for a 1996 or newer vehicle.
evIncentiveDetails: Efficiency Maine offers income-qualified EV rebates when paired with an off-peak charger: $7,000 new / $3,000 used for low-income buyers and $5,000 new / $2,000 used for moderate-income buyers.
registrationNotes: Excise tax is paid to the municipality.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Maryland
description: Maryland requires liability insurance, safety inspections for vehicle transfers, and has a strong lemon law. The state mandates emissions testing and offers growing EV incentive programs.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $15,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Maryland's lemon law is Md. Code, Com. Law §§ 14-1501 and 14-1502. For this statute the manufacturer's warranty period is the earlier of 18,000 miles or 24 months after delivery. The presumption is four repairs of the same problem, 30 or more days out of service, or one repair of a brake or steering failure that still will not pass the state safety inspection after the manufacturer had a chance to cure. Report the problem by certified mail, return receipt requested, and the manufacturer is supposed to finish the corrections within 30 days of getting that letter.
emissionsDetails: Eligible vehicles in the VEIP counties are tested every two years. A qualifying new vehicle is first tested 72 months from the model year. The test fee is $30, or $26 at a self-serve kiosk. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: Maryland requires a safety inspection when a vehicle is sold or the ownership changes.
evIncentiveDetails: Maryland's EV excise tax credit currently has no funding; applicants are placed on a waiting list.
registrationNotes: Those registration amounts include the $40 EMS surcharge. A registration may be renewed for two or three years. Excise tax is 6.5 percent of fair market value.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A battery-electric vehicle pays a $125 annual surcharge. A plug-in hybrid pays $100 a year.

name: Massachusetts
description: Massachusetts requires an annual safety inspection. A vehicle that runs only on electricity does not take the emissions portion. The state has strong consumer protections and EV incentive programs.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $20,000 bodily injury per person / $40,000 bodily injury per accident / $5,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Massachusetts calls the coverage a term of protection of one year or 15,000 miles in Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 90, § 7N 1/2, and a business day is a day the authorized dealers' service departments are normally open. Three repairs of the same problem that continues or comes back, or 15 business days out of service, is a reasonable number of attempts. The manufacturer gets one more chance to cure, and that extra chance cannot run longer than seven business days. The buyer does not have to notify the manufacturer directly before using the state's certified new-car arbitration.
emissionsDetails: A light-duty nondiesel vehicle is exempt when its model year is earlier than 1996 or the vehicle is 15 or more model years old. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test. The vehicle still needs the annual safety inspection.
safetyInspectionDetails: Massachusetts requires an annual safety inspection for every registered vehicle. The inspection is $35 for most vehicles. A vehicle operated only on electricity still needs the safety inspection.
evIncentiveDetails: Massachusetts MOR-EV pays $3,500 for new battery EVs with an MSRP up to $55,000 and for income-eligible used EVs, plus $1,500 MOR-EV+ for income-qualified residents and a $1,000 trade-in bonus (mor-ev.org).
registrationNotes: Registration is biennial. A 6.25 percent sales tax applies to a purchase.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Michigan
description: Michigan is a no-fault insurance state with unique auto insurance requirements. As the heart of the American auto industry, the state has comprehensive vehicle laws and strong consumer protections.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $50,000 bodily injury per person / $100,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / PIP coverage required
lemonLawSummary: Michigan's lemon law, Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 257.1402 and 257.1403, asks the owner to report the defect during the express warranty or within one year of delivery, whichever is earlier, and it sets no mileage cap. The presumption is four repairs of the same defect within two years of the first repair attempt, or 30 days out of service during the warranty or that first year. After the third repair, send written notice by return receipt; the manufacturer then has five business days to repair. On the days-out path, written notice goes out after 25 days in the shop, and the manufacturer again has five business days.
registrationFeeRange: Based on the vehicle's list price
registrationNotes: The first registration of a passenger vehicle from model year 1984 or newer is set by list price under MCL 257.801. The tax is $36 when the list price is $6,000 or less. Above $6,000 the tax steps by $6 for each $1,000 of list price. Above $30,000 the tax is $178 plus $6 for each $1,000 or fraction over $30,000. The second registration is 90 percent of the first. The third is 90 percent of the second. Later registrations stay at 90 percent of the third. List price is the base list price published by the secretary of state, or the price on the window label when that list is not published. The Michigan Secretary of State fee chart follows this statute.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A vehicle that runs only on electricity and weighs 8,000 pounds or less has a statutory add-on of $100. The add-on rises with the gasoline tax above 19 cents a gallon under MCL 257.801.

name: Minnesota
description: Minnesota requires liability insurance and has a no-fault insurance component. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and offers growing incentives for EV adoption.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / $40,000 PIP
lemonLawSummary: Minn. Stat. § 325F.665 places the presumption in the express warranty or in the two years after delivery, and the date that comes first ends it. Miles do not shorten that window. A problem first reported while the warranty was still running can still support a refund or replacement from attempts made within three years of delivery. The presumption is four repairs, 30 business days out of service, or a single repair of a complete brake or steering failure that is likely to cause death or serious injury, and the four-repair and 30-day routes need written notice plus a chance to cure.
emissionsDetails: Minnesota's Twin Cities auto emissions inspection program ended on March 1, 2000, when the Legislature repealed it. The state does not require an emissions test to register a vehicle.
evIncentiveDetails: Minnesota's EV rebate funding is currently exhausted.
registrationNotes: The percentage applies to a vehicle first registered in Minnesota on or after November 16, 2020. The share of MSRP falls with age. From the 11th year the amount added to the base is $20.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle pays a surcharge of $150, or a greater amount based on age and MSRP.

name: Mississippi
description: Mississippi requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles and has a lemon law for new vehicle purchases. The state does not require emissions testing or annual safety inspections.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Miss. Code Ann. § 63-17-159 keeps the repair presumption inside the express warranty or the first year after delivery, whichever finishes sooner. The section does not add a mileage limit. Substantially the same problem repaired three times, or 15 working days in the shop for that problem, is enough, and routine maintenance is not part of the 15 days. Write the manufacturer before you rely on the section; once the car is at the shop the manufacturer names, that shop has ten working days to make it conform.
registrationFeeRange: $12.75 to renew or $14 for a first registration
registrationNotes: A passenger vehicle also pays a $15 privilege tax. Local ad valorem tax is charged as well.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Missouri
description: Missouri requires liability insurance. Safety inspections are biennial, with an exemption for many newer low-mileage vehicles. Emissions testing applies in the St. Louis area and not in Kansas City. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Under Mo. Rev. Stat. §§ 407.565 and 407.571, the clock runs for the express warranty or for one year after delivery, and the period that ends first controls. There is no mileage cutoff in that test. The same problem repaired four times, or the car held for repair for 30 working days, meets the presumption, and days spent on ordinary maintenance stay out of the count. Tell the manufacturer or its agent about the problem before that window closes.
emissionsDetails: The Gateway Vehicle Inspection Program tests gasoline vehicles from model year 1996 and diesel vehicles from model year 1997, at or under 8,500 pounds, that are registered in St. Louis City or in St. Louis, St. Charles, or Jefferson County. Franklin County residents have been exempt since July 1, 2022. Kansas City is not in the program. The state cap on the emissions inspection fee is $24. Even model years are tested in even calendar years, and odd model years in odd calendar years. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: RSMo § 307.350 requires a biennial safety inspection, in the even calendar year for an even model year and in the odd calendar year for an odd model year, and also when ownership changes. A vehicle is exempt for the first ten model years if it has fewer than 150,000 miles, other than a prior salvage vehicle right after it is rebuilt. The certificate is generally valid for 60 days. The Department of Revenue said on January 6, 2026, that these rules had not changed.
registrationNotes: A $9 processing fee is added to a one-year registration.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Montana
description: Montana is popular for vehicle registration due to its lack of sales tax. The state requires liability insurance but does not mandate emissions testing or safety inspections for most vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Montana defines the warranty period in Mont. Code Ann. §§ 61-4-501 and 61-4-504 as two years or 18,000 miles, whichever is earlier. The presumption is four repairs of the same problem, or 30 business days out of service after the manufacturer, its agent, or a dealer was notified. Send written notice to the manufacturer or its agent while the warranty period is still open. The manufacturer has to tell the buyer that written notice is required, and the presumption is not used against a manufacturer that never received that notice and a chance to cure.
registrationFeeRange: $217 at 0 to 4 years, $87 at 5 to 10 years, or $28 at 11 years or older
registrationNotes: A county option tax is also charged.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Nebraska
description: Nebraska requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing and has a motor vehicle tax based on vehicle value.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 60-2704 times the presumption to the express warranty or to one year after delivery, and the earlier of those two dates ends it. The statute does not set a mileage limit. The car meets the test after four repairs of the same problem or after 40 days out of service. That test is available only once the manufacturer has notice by certified mail and a chance to cure.
registrationNotes: The motor vehicle tax is based on MSRP and age.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric or hydrogen passenger vehicle pays a $150 alternative-fuel fee. A plug-in electric passenger vehicle pays $75.

name: Nevada
description: Nevada requires liability insurance and emissions testing in the Las Vegas and Reno metro areas. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and offers growing EV incentive programs.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Nevada asks the buyer to report the problem in writing under NRS 597.610 before the express warranty ends or one year after delivery to the original buyer, whichever is earlier. NRS 597.630 then presumes enough attempts after four repairs of the same problem or 30 calendar days out of service. The 30-day count can run longer when the needed repair is delayed for reasons outside the manufacturer's or dealer's control.
emissionsDetails: Qualifying gasoline vehicles based in urban Clark County or Washoe County need an annual test beginning with the fourth registration. The 2026 maximum for a light-duty gasoline test is $75.50 in Clark County and $71.50 in Washoe County. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
registrationNotes: Governmental services tax is based on the vehicle's value.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: New Hampshire
description: New Hampshire does not require drivers to carry auto insurance, though they remain financially responsible for damages. The DMV's February 13, 2026 guidance suspends the vehicle inspection program until further notice.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage. Note: Insurance is not mandatory in New Hampshire, but these minimums apply if you carry coverage.
lemonLawSummary: New Hampshire's presumption in RSA 357-D:3, VII is measured during the express warranty. Three repairs of the same problem, or 30 business days out of service, meets the presumption, counting a business day as a day those dealers normally keep a service department open. Repair attempts should be on written repair orders, generally at the same dealer, and a car the owner can use for a major part of the day is not out of service. After the third repair or after those 30 business days, RSA 357-D:4 requires written notice to the manufacturer, which then gets one final chance to repair.
safetyInspectionDetails: The New Hampshire DMV's February 13, 2026 guidance says the vehicle inspection program is suspended until further notice. Stations are not issuing state inspection stickers, and an annual inspection is not required while that suspension stands. Drivers remain responsible for the equipment rules in RSA 266. OBD emissions testing was part of that inspection. The status can change.
registrationFeeRange: $42 up to 3,000 lb, $48 from 3,001 to 5,000 lb, or $66 from 5,001 to 8,000 lb
registrationNotes: The town or city also charges a permit fee. There is no sales tax on the purchase.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: New Jersey
description: New Jersey requires no-fault insurance with some of the highest minimum coverage requirements in the nation. The state mandates emissions testing and has strong consumer protection laws.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $15,000 bodily injury per person / $30,000 bodily injury per accident / $5,000 property damage / $15,000 PIP
lemonLawSummary: New Jersey's lemon law, N.J.S.A. 56:12-33, uses the first 24,000 miles or two years, and a motorhome uses 45 calendar days out of service where a passenger car uses 20. Three repairs of substantially the same problem, that days-out total, or one exam of a problem likely to cause death or serious injury, is the presumption. It applies only after the manufacturer received certified-mail notice, return receipt requested, and had one chance to repair within 10 calendar days. That letter may go out after two repairs, after the car has been out 20 calendar days (45 for a motorhome), or after one exam of a serious safety problem.
emissionsDetails: New Jersey requires biennial emissions inspections for most vehicles 5+ model years old. Testing is performed at state Motor Vehicle Commission inspection stations at no charge. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
evIncentiveDetails: Charge Up New Jersey offers $1,500 at the dealer for an eligible new EV, or $4,000 total for income-qualified Charge Up+ applicants, plus up to $250 toward a home Level 2 charger.
registrationFeeRange: $46.50 or $59 under 3,500 lb, and $71.50 or $84 above 3,500 lb
registrationNotes: The lower amount in each pair is for a model older than two years. The higher amount is for a model within two years.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A zero-emission vehicle pays an added annual fee of $250 beginning July 1, 2024. That fee rises by $10 a year for four years.

name: New Mexico
description: New Mexico requires liability insurance for all registered vehicles. The state has emissions testing in the Albuquerque area and a lemon law covering new vehicle purchases.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: NMSA 1978 § 57-16A-3(C) covers a new vehicle for the express warranty or for the year after delivery, and the presumption follows the date that arrives first. Miles are not a separate cutoff. Four repairs that leave the same problem uncorrected, or 30 business days the car sits with the manufacturer, an agent, or a dealer, meets the test, not counting routine maintenance. Direct written notice and a chance to cure have to come first, and the manufacturer must say so in the warranty or in a separate notice.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing applies to vehicles registered or commuting in Bernalillo County. Vehicles from 1991 and newer, up to 10,000 pounds, are tested every two years and at a change of ownership. A brand-new vehicle is exempt for four years after the first registration on the manufacturer certificate of origin. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
registrationFeeRange: Based on shipping weight and years registered
registrationNotes: Chapter 4 of the 2026 laws set the twelve-month fees. After five years of registration the fees are $26.25, $38.75, and $56.25. Before that they are $33.75, $48.75, and $70. Each registration includes a $1.50 tire recycling fee.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An additional electric-vehicle fee of $70 starts on January 1, 2027.

name: New York
description: New York has comprehensive vehicle ownership requirements including no-fault insurance, annual safety and emissions inspections, and one of the strongest lemon laws in the nation.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $10,000 property damage / $50,000 PIP (no-fault) required
lemonLawSummary: New York's general presumption in General Business Law § 198-a(d) covers the first 18,000 miles or two years. Four repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service, is the test for a car. During that period, report the problem to the manufacturer, its agent, or an authorized dealer, and the agent or dealer has seven days to forward written notice by certified mail. Motor homes in the same section follow a different path: certified-mail notice after two repairs or 21 days out of service, and the owner may proceed after three repairs or 30 days out, if the manufacturer gave prior written notice of that requirement.
emissionsDetails: Annual emissions testing is required statewide as part of the annual safety inspection for most vehicles 2+ model years old. OBD-II testing is used for 1996+ model year vehicles. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for all registered vehicles. Inspections cover brakes, steering, tires, lights, glass, exhaust, and emissions. Cost varies by shop but is typically $10-$37.
evIncentiveDetails: NYSERDA's Drive Clean Rebate takes $500 to $2,000 off eligible new EVs at participating dealers, based on range and MSRP. Utilities such as Con Edison offer additional charging programs.
registrationNotes: The weight schedule is the two-year fee. New York City residents also pay a supplemental registration fee. Sales tax varies by county.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: North Carolina
description: North Carolina requires liability insurance and an annual safety inspection statewide. Emissions testing remains in 19 counties until EPA approves the end of that program.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $30,000 bodily injury per person / $60,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: North Carolina allows a refund or replacement under N.C.G.S. § 20-351.3 for a defect that substantially impairs value and showed up no later than 24 months or 24,000 miles after delivery. The presumption in § 20-351.5 is four repairs of the same problem that still exists, or 20 business days out of service during any 12-month period of the warranty. Express warranties have to last at least one year or 12,000 miles, and the repair duty runs for one year or the express-warranty term, whichever is longer. Notify the manufacturer directly in writing and allow up to 15 calendar days to correct the problem, unless it never disclosed that written notice was required; § 20-351.7 also requires a separate 10-day written notice before you sue.
emissionsDetails: Emissions testing is part of the annual inspection in 19 counties. Session Law 2023-134 and Session Law 2026-41 end that emissions program after EPA approval, and the annual safety inspection remains statewide. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take this emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: North Carolina requires an annual safety inspection statewide for registered vehicles. The emissions portion, where it still applies, is limited to 19 counties and is separate from the statewide safety inspection.
registrationNotes: Registration and licensing are annual.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A plug-in electric vehicle that uses no other power source pays an additional $214.50. A plug-in hybrid pays an additional $107.25.

name: North Dakota
description: North Dakota requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing or safety inspections and has some of the lowest insurance rates in the nation.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: N.D.C.C. § 51-07-19 measures repairs during the express warranty or during the year after delivery, and the shorter of those two periods is the one that counts. There is no mileage cap on that presumption. More than three repairs of the same problem, which means a fourth visit while the trouble is still present, or 30 business days out of service, is the presumption. It does not run against the manufacturer until the manufacturer has had direct notice and a chance to cure.
registrationNotes: The 2026 schedule uses weight and the year first registered, not the model year.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle pays an additional $120 road-use fee. A plug-in hybrid pays an additional $50.

name: Ohio
description: Ohio requires liability insurance but is unique in that it uses a financial responsibility law rather than mandatory insurance. The state requires emissions testing in certain urban counties.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Ohio's lemon law, Ohio Rev. Code § 1345.73, uses the first year or 18,000 miles, whichever is earlier, the same window § 1345.72 uses for reporting a repair. Three repairs of substantially the same problem, 30 calendar days out of service, eight attempts to repair any problems, or one attempt at a problem likely to cause death or serious bodily injury, is enough if the problem continues or comes back. Report the nonconformity to the manufacturer, its agent, or its authorized dealer during that year or 18,000 miles.
emissionsDetails: E-Check applies in Cuyahoga, Geauga, Lake, Lorain, Medina, Portage, and Summit counties. Gasoline and diesel vehicles that are 6 to 25 years old, and non-plug-in hybrids that are 7 to 25 years old, are tested every two years at 10,000 pounds or less. An established Ohio resident gets one free passing test in 365 days. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
registrationNotes: The deputy registrar fee for one year is $8. County permissive tax cannot exceed $30. A replacement plate is $15 for one plate or $16.25 for two. A hybrid pays an additional $100 a year.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An electric vehicle pays an additional $200 a year. A plug-in hybrid pays an additional $150 a year.

name: Oklahoma
description: Oklahoma requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing but mandates personal property taxes on vehicles, known as excise tax.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: 15 O.S. § 901(D) places Oklahoma's presumption inside the express warranty or the year after delivery, and the period that ends first is the one that applies. Mileage is not part of that cutoff. The same problem repaired four times, or 30 business days in the shop, creates the presumption. Put the report in writing to the manufacturer during the warranty or that year; without that notice and a chance to cure, the presumption does not apply.
registrationFeeRange: Based on the year of registration
registrationNotes: The fee is $96 for registration years 1 through 4. It then steps down to $26 from year 17 on. The motor vehicle excise tax is 3.25 percent of vehicle value.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Oregon
description: Oregon has no sales tax on vehicle purchases and requires emissions testing in the Portland metro area. The state has a strong lemon law and offers significant incentives for electric vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $20,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Oregon's lemon law, ORS 646A.406, uses two years after delivery or 24,000 miles, whichever ends first. The presumption is three repairs plus a chance to cure, 30 calendar days out of service (60 for a motor home), or one repair plus a final attempt on a problem likely to cause death or serious injury, if the problem continues. Before the presumption is used, the manufacturer needs a direct letter about the defect and a chance to correct it.
emissionsDetails: Non-exempt passenger vehicles in the Portland and Medford areas are tested every two years. The DEQ test fee is $25 in Portland and $20 in Medford, and only after a passing result. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
evIncentiveDetails: Oregon's Clean Vehicle Rebate covers purchases and leases from August 25 to November 4, 2026 only, and funds are running low; late applications may be waitlisted until spring 2027. Oregon has no sales tax on vehicle purchases.
registrationFeeRange: $126 at 0 to 19 MPG, $136 at 20 to 39 MPG, or $216 at 40 MPG or higher
registrationNotes: A new passenger vehicle with a manufacturer certificate of origin is registered for four years, and that registration fee is doubled. Multnomah County adds $112. Washington County and Clackamas County add $60.
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: An all-electric passenger vehicle that is not enrolled in OReGO pays $376 for two years. The title fee for that vehicle is $192. The miles-per-gallon schedule does not apply.

name: Pennsylvania
description: Pennsylvania requires liability insurance and annual safety and emissions inspections. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and is part of a multi-state emissions standards agreement.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $15,000 bodily injury per person / $30,000 bodily injury per accident / $5,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Pennsylvania's Automobile Lemon Law, the Act of March 28, 1984, P.L. 150, No. 28, covers a car for one year, 12,000 miles, or the warranty, whichever comes first. A motorcycle uses one year or the warranty, and the statute does not add a mileage cap for motorcycles. Three repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service, is the presumption in section 6. When the car comes back to the same dealer a second time for the same problem, section 7 says the dealer notifies the manufacturer by certified mail within seven days.
emissionsDetails: Annual emissions testing is required in 25 counties. The emissions sticker has no state fee. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: Annual safety inspections are required for every registered vehicle. The official inspection sticker fee is $12.
registrationNotes: A 6 percent sales tax applies to a purchase.
lemonLawCitation: Automobile Lemon Law, Act of Mar. 28, 1984, P.L. 150, No. 28, § 6
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).

name: Rhode Island
description: Rhode Island requires liability insurance and biennial safety and emissions inspections. The state has a lemon law for new vehicles and eliminated the car excise tax in recent years.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: Rhode Island's term of protection in R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-5.2-1 is one year or 15,000 miles, and the presumption is in § 31-5.2-5. Four repairs of the same problem, or 30 calendar days out of service, during that term is the test, and the manufacturer also gets one more cure of not more than seven calendar days. Report the nonconformity during the term of protection. The extra seven days starts when the manufacturer first knows the four-repair or 30-day limit has been met.
emissionsDetails: Gas and diesel light-duty vehicles take the emissions test with the safety inspection every 24 months. A new vehicle is exempt for two years from purchase or until 24,000 miles, whichever comes first. A vehicle operated only on electricity does not take the emissions test.
safetyInspectionDetails: A light-duty vehicle of 8,500 pounds or less must pass a safety and emissions inspection at least once every 24 months. The fee for that inspection is $55.
registrationFeeRange: $30 a year up to 4,000 lb gross weight
registrationNotes: A two-year passenger renewal also adds a $3.50 technology surcharge for each year. It adds a $20 department of transportation surcharge for each year. A plug-in hybrid pays an additional $100 per registration year. A non-plug-in hybrid pays an additional $50 per registration year.
lemonLawCitation: R.I. Gen. Laws § 31-5.2-5; term of protection defined in § 31-5.2-1
averageInsuranceSource: The 2024 combined average for liability, collision, and comprehensive in Table 5 of the NAIC Auto Insurance Database Average Premium Supplement (https://content.naic.org/sites/default/files/2024-adb-average-premium-supplement.pdf).
evRegistrationDetails: A battery-electric vehicle pays an additional $200 per registration year.

name: South Carolina
description: South Carolina requires liability insurance and has a lemon law for new vehicles. The state does not require emissions testing or annual safety inspections and has a low personal property tax on vehicles.
insuranceMinimumDetail: $25,000 bodily injury per person / $50,000 bodily injury per accident / $25,000 property damage
lemonLawSummary: South Carolina, in S.C. Code §§ 56-28-30 and 56-28-40, asks for a report within the first 12 months or 12,000 miles, while the presumption counts repairs and days during the express warranty. The presumption is met by three repairs aimed at the same problem, or by 30 calendar days the car spends out of service. If the manufacturer clearly said at the sale that written notice is required, send that notice so it can make a final repair. It then has ten business days to name a franchised shop and ten business days after delivery to attempt the repair.
registrationNotes: The infrastructure maintenance fee is 5 percent of the purchase price and is capped at $500. Personal property tax is also assessed.
